experiences.name: Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse
experiences.description: A squat 1903 limestone lighthouse at the tip of the cape, run by the Capes Foundation. Guided tours climb 59 steps to the balcony for 360-degree views over Geographe Bay and the Indian Ocean, and the surrounding trails are prime whale-spotting territory from September to December.

briefing.icebreaker: At just over 20 metres it is one of Australia's shortest lighthouses, yet its clifftop perch makes its light visible some 25 nautical miles out to sea.
briefing.proMove: Tours run on the hour from 9am; book the first slot and walk a stretch of the Cape to Cape Track before the coaches arrive.
briefing.hiddenGem: The free whale lookout deck a short stroll from the lighthouse is one of the best land-based humpback viewing points in WA.

experiences.sommNote: Climb it before a Yallingup tasting; the sea air sharpens the palate wonderfully.

experiences.name: Margaret River Golf Club
experiences.description: An 18-hole course threaded through native bushland on Wallcliffe Road, minutes from Margaret River town. Kangaroos graze the fairways at dawn and dusk, and visitors are welcome with essential bookings.

briefing.icebreaker: You will almost certainly share a fairway with a mob of western grey kangaroos here.
briefing.proMove: Bookings are essential; reserve online via the club's tee-time calendar before you travel.
briefing.hiddenGem: It is officially a private members' club, yet visitors are warmly welcomed — a green fee buys you one of WA's top-rated country courses, only 7 km from the town centre.

experiences.sommNote: Nine relaxed holes here is the classic palate-reset between Wallcliffe cellar doors.
